blocks.text: J. D. Michaelis proposed another etymology in Supplemm. ad Lexx. Hebrr. vol. 2, p. 416. He thinks that the Hebrew name of the hoopoe, דוכיפת, is compounded from דו, Arabic ذو [dhū], en- [III, 109] dowed with, having, and Chaldee כִיפָה, ambergris, so that this bird would be called endowed with ambergris ironically, on account of its dungy smell. But Tychsen rightly says on the Physiologus Syrus, Chapter 22, §3, p. 119: "The etymology is indeed ingenious, if only it were true. For the report that the hoopoe feeds on human excrement and builds its nest from it is very unreliable, and arose from a deception of the senses. For it does not feed on excrement, but, like hens, searches through it diligently for seeds or insects, sometimes carrying away a strong smell from it, as I often noticed in a hoopoe which I had given as a companion to my hens at Bützow. Otherwise it was clean of smell, and fed on insects, berries of black elder, red currant, gooseberry, raspberry, vine, etc., and on seeds of garlic, leek, celery, etc." So Tychsen; and this is also confirmed by Buffon, Hist. Nat. des oiseaux, vol. 6, p. 439 f., and by Oedmann, part 5, ch. 7, p. 71. But the etymology proposed by Michaelis is also opposed by the fact that neither דו nor כִיפָה is a Hebrew word: one is Arabic, the other Chaldee. Nor is Oedmann's opinion any more acceptable, who thinks that דוכיפת is compounded from דוך, cock, and יפה, beautiful, since יְפַת is used only in the construct state. Preferable, therefore, seems the etymology that Bochart put in first place, that דוכיפת is properly the mountain cock, or wild cock.
Book 1, ch. 16, p. 112 etc., and book 2, ch. 27, p. 321.

Lest anyone think that there was no need to forbid the eating of this bird, it should be pointed out that it can be eaten if the head is cut off at once, as Michaelis reports from Salerne's Ornithol. vol. 3, p. 690, in Supplemm. ad Lexx. Hebrr. vol. 2, p. 417, where he has quoted Salerne's own words. To him I add Aldrovandi, Ornithol. vol. 2, p. 709: I have often come across it (the hoopoe) for sale in the market, and I have observed that it is bought by many, and learned that it is recommended.
